label: Intercompany governance
query: How should intercompany lending be governed so Lakeshore avoids sloppy AFR and true-up failures?
answer: Lakeshore already has the bones for this in place — SAP S/4HANA intercompany at Holdco and key opcos — but you don’t yet have a consistent governance spine across banners. To stay out of AFR/true‑up trouble, I’d anchor on four things: 1) Make “intercompany lending” a single owned product Assign a Holdco Intercompany Owner (as your ERP object already assumes) with explicit authority over: – Policy (who can lend/borrow, tenors, rates, FX rules, minimum documentation) – Process design across ERP-LSH-HOLDCO-INTERCOMPANY, ERP-NLS-INTERCOMPANY, ERP-BMS-INTERCOMPANY, ERP-FFF-INTERCOMPANY, ERP-GLP-INTERCOMPANY – Exception approvals 2) Fix the booking model at the source Non‑negotiables: – Every intercompany loan/advance is created via a standard S/4HANA / ECC / NetSuite object with a unique global deal ID, not ad‑hoc journal entries. – Mirror entries must be system‑enforced (borrower and lender created in a single workflow). – Standard interest and FX policies owned by Treasury (ties directly to your cash_forecast_accuracy and treasury visibility board priority). 3) Put quarterly AFR and true‑up on rails – Close calendar: lock in intercompany confirmation windows per quarter, with a hard gate before group AFR sign‑off. – Automated reconciliations: use S/4HANA intercompany and NetSuite matching rules to flag mismatches in principal, interest, and FX; issue exception reports by BU (Northline, Brightmark, Forge & Field, Great Lakes Pantry, Holdco). – Escalation ladder: if a pair doesn’t reconcile by T+2 of close, it escalates to BU CFOs, and then Holdco CFO at T+3.
